lede: What I can show, how, and what I cannot. Numbers in the first block are read from the project at the commit shown. The recorded runs below are dated results of commands I ran, not live numbers.

recorded_runs.what: Twelve-minute demo script, every typed command run by a test
recorded_runs.command: uv run --frozen pytest -p no:cacheprovider on the long-form demo test file

claims.claim: Permissions live on the lever, not the model
Edits to the audit log are detected
claims.evidence: Hash chain with head pin; browser verifier agrees with the Python one
claims.tests: tests/phase1/test_audit.py, tests/py/audit/test_b17_audit_v2.py, site chain parity test

claims.claim: A requester-verified change is refused without a callback
A hostile ticket gets no lever
claims.state: proven on a 50-case corpus written with the rules

claims.claim: Each client is isolated from the others
Rollback proposes the registered undo only when state matches the record
The summary numbers in the baseline report match the findings

not_proven: Anything against a real tenant, real tickets or real users.
Real Microsoft sign-in. The issuer is a mock; claim names follow public documentation and are unchecked against a live token.
The two-approver rule on the shipped page. It is enforced and tested in the runner only.
Model quality. The classifier is a deterministic mock and the labels share an author with the rules.
Vendor field names and enum values for PSA, backup, alerts and device tools. They are neutral placeholders.
Production behaviour: load, failure, throttling, and the single-writer limit of the audit log.
That the guard hooks fire in every live assistant session.
